statement: Use the trapezium rule with 4 strips to estimate $I=\\int_{0}^{1}e^{-x^{2}}\,dx$. Given that $|f''(x)|\\le2$ on $[0,1]$, state an upper bound for the error of your estimate.
solution: With $h=1/4$ the nodes are $x=0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1$ and $f(x)=e^{-x^{2}}$ takes values $1,\,e^{-0.0625}\\approx0.9394,\,e^{-0.25}\\approx0.7788,\,e^{-0.5625}\\approx0.5698,\,e^{-1}\\approx0.3679$. The trapezium estimate is $\\frac{h}{2}\bigl[f_{0}+2(f_{1}+f_{2}+f_{3})+f_{4}\\bigr]=\\frac{1}{8}\bigl[1+2(0.9394+0.7788+0.5698)+0.3679\\bigr]\\approx0.7430$. The trapezium error satisfies $|E|\\le\\frac{(b-a)h^{2}}{12}\\max|f''|$; with $\\max|f''|\\le2$ this gives $|E|\\le\\frac{1\\cdot(1/4)^{2}}{12}\\cdot2=\\frac{1}{96}\\approx0.0104$.
hints: List the five function values at the four strip boundaries.
Use the error bound (b-a)h^2/12 times max|f''|.
